settings.title: Succession and continuity planning for Filipino family businesses

settings.editor: A holistic, integrated process covering wealth, estate, organization and succession, with family unity kept at the centre of every decision.

Family enterprise planning is the process of deciding, documenting and rehearsing how leadership and ownership of a family-owned company pass to the next generation. It covers three handovers that are often confused: management, ownership, and the family authority behind both. A complete plan names successors, sets a timetable, protects and transfers assets, and defines how the family will resolve disagreement.

settings.title: Why the plan matters more than the document.

settings.editor: A short word from our consultants on what changes for a family once the plan is agreed, and why the conversation has to come before the paperwork.
We help build the family’s culture: shared values, trust, and the habit of talking openly.
We guide the family in crafting its family constitution and deciding who leads next.
We help the family protect its assets and plan how its estate and shares will pass.
We facilitate family council meetings and establish a governance rhythm that lasts.
A comprehensive plan to reach the family’s financial goals.

settings.title: Documents the family can hold, sign and revisit.

settings.editor:

  • A development plan for the next generation of leaders

settings.title: When should a family business start succession planning?

settings.editor: While the founder still has the authority to make an unpopular decision stick. Once illness, a dispute or an outside offer sets the timetable, the range of workable options has already narrowed.

settings.title: How is this different from estate planning?

settings.editor: Estate planning decides how assets pass and what tax is due. Succession planning decides who runs and who owns the business. Families that do one without the other find the gap at the worst moment.
About 196 hours of facilitated work, roughly 24.5 days, from the first family orientation to the ceremonial signing of the plan. See the full breakdown in our FAQs.
